overview: This event ties together t-6b vn diagram, maneuvering speed, and acceleration limitations in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

items.text: Maneuvering Speed is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.

children.text: Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
Max speed where full control deflection will not overstress the aircraft.
abrupt/full control movement in one axis may cause structural damage.
Full rudder deflection > 150 KIAS exceeds system limits.
Reference figure 5-4 in the NATOPS page 5-10 (Vn Diagram above)

items.text: abrupt/full control movement in one axis may cause structural damage.

children.text: Full or abrupt multi-axis inputs can overstress even below VO.

items.text: Treat this as a cumulative EP brief. The instructor can move quickly between recognition, memory items, and the branch logic that decides whether you continue, land, or eject.

children.text: Emergency Engine Shutdown on the Ground
Be able to state the recognition cue before you recite the steps.
Know the associated N/W/Cs, not just the memory items.
Have a clear answer for when the EP becomes a PEL, forced-landing, or ejection problem.

studyNotes.summary: Keep T-6B Vn Diagram and Maneuvering Speed organized early, then know the immediate actions, branch logic, and N/W/C details before you start improvising.
